ops.en: THE DESCENT SEALED [G62-01/08/09]. ve-yosef HURAD mitzrayma — the was-brought-down skeleton stands twice in the Torah: Joseph here, and 'take DOWN your ornaments' (Exod 33:5) [VERIFIED: manifest G62-08]; and horiduhu ('they brought him down') pairs exactly with 44:21's 'bring him down to me' — the Kitzur's measure-for-measure [VERIFIED: G62-09]. The buyer: POTIPHAR — one written word, full yod and…
THE REFRAIN. va-yehi YHWH et yosef va-yehi ish matzliach — the prosper-word opens and closes the chapter (39:2, 3, 23): the machine's only stable fact across the fall.

THE ACCOMPANIMENT FORMULA FRAMES THE CHAPTER [claim G62-14, machine-checked]. "The LORD was with Joseph" stands at 39:2 and 39:3 in the master's house and again at 39:21 and 39:23 in the prison — two before the fall and two after, an exact frame around the accusation. The received translation renders each with its Word-as-support formula, the same idiom it uses of Jacob at 48:21 and in Joseph's bl…

THE MASTER'S READING. va-yar adonav ki YHWH ito — the master sees the Name by its works: be-yado, in JOSEPH'S hand — the hand-word the chapter will pass from prosperity (39:3) to seized garment (39:12) to the warden's trust (39:22).

HIS TONGUE IN THE FINALS [G62-05]. ve-khal yesh lo natan be-yado — the five words' closing letters spell leshono ('his TONGUE') [VERIFIED: manifest G62-05]: the Kitzur — Gabriel taught him seventy tongues, and so he prospered; the acrostic sits exactly on the handover clause.

THE SPILLOVER. va-yevarekh YHWH et bet ha-mitzri BI-GELAL yosef — the for-the-sake-of blessing: Laban's discovery (30:27) repeated in Egypt; the bless-thread runs through the foreign houses that hold this family.

THE HINGE. va-yehi yosef yefe toar vi-yfe mare — his mother's exact double epithet (29:17, Rachel) handed to the son at the verse-seam before the trial; yefe joined by maqqef without a stress-stroke in the precise books (MS, named). The bread-clause (the Kitzur's letter-sum reading: 'the bread he ate' = his wife) files named.

THE TWO-WORD DEMAND. shikhva imi — pushed, and NEVER discharged: the span ends with it still open on the queue under a standing refusal — the machine's record of a demand held at bay rather than resolved. The paragraph question rides the verse-head: Sephardic precise books write NO break here; Rambam and the Hilleli make it open; the Meiri leaves an undecided gap [VERIFIED: manifest G62-12, camps …

THE REFUSAL DRAWN OUT [G62-04]. va-yemaEN — the chain-accent (shalshelet) hangs on the refusal-verb, one of the whole Torah's FOUR chain-stations [VERIFIED: manifest G62-04]: Bachya's principle is stated on this word — from the accents we understand what is not written, as from a man's gestures we know his heart: the mark stretches the refusal to its utmost (the tradition hears the struggle inside…

THE THREE FENCES. ve-ekh eese ha-raa ha-gedola ha-zot ve-chatati le- ELOHIM — the master's trust, the wife's status, and God: the refusal climbs to the Name. ha-ze with the zayin dagesheed per MS [G62-10, asserted].

THE STANDING REFUSAL. ke-dabrah el yosef YOM YOM ve-lo shama eleha — the open demand renewed daily and daily refused: the machine holds the queue steady while the letter counts the days. The Kitzur's letter-sum on 'to be with her' (= into Gehenna) files named.

THE CLEARED STAGE. ve-en ish me-anshe ha-bayit sham ba-bayit — the house-word tolls three times in the verse; melakhto ('his work') — the same word the Sabbath rested (2:2-3) and Joseph's only other Torah-station carried (39:11 is מלאכתו tok4 of 4, gen_07's census closing HERE): the last his-work in the Torah is the errand into the empty house.

THE EMPTY HOUSE AND THE FATHER'S IMAGE [claim G62-13]. "He came into the house to do his work" is read three ways in the chain — his actual accounts, an INDEED (he came for her), and "no man of the household there" because all had gone to the Nile festival or the theatre. The received translation votes for the first, rendering the errand as checking the account-books; the reading adds the restrain…

THE DEMAND SEIZES. va-titpesehu BE-VIGDO lemor shikhva imi — the two-word demand pushed a second time, now with a hand on the cloth; both pushes stay open: the queue carries the doubled refusal to the span's end.

THE THIRD GARMENT-CODE. va-yaazov bigdo be-yadah va-yanas — the coat stripped (37:23), the veil swapped (38:14), now the cloak abandoned: three units, three garments doing the narrative's lying and truth- telling; bigdo runs six times through this chapter, always as evidence.
THE EVIDENCE INVERTED. ki-reotah ki azav bigdo be-yadah — she reads the abandoned cloth as her script: the chapter's hand-word now holds the lie.

THE FIRST TELLING. reu hevi LANU ish ivri le-tzacheq BANU — she indicts her own husband ('he brought us') and borrows the mock-verb of Lot's sons-in-law and Ishmael (19:14, 21:9): the laughter-word's dark track. Her cry is claimed, not narrated: the letter records only her report of it.

THE RAISED HAND AND THE RAISED VOICE [G62-07]. HARIMOTI qoli — the I-raised word stands exactly twice in the Torah: Abram's hand lifted in the oath that refused Sodom's spoil (14:22), and this voice lifted in the false cry [VERIFIED: manifest G62-07]: the same word carries an oath and a lie.
THE STAGED CLOTH. va-tanach bigdo ETZLAH — the garment rests beside her as the coat rested before Jacob: the third unit running whose central witness is cloth.

THE RETELLING'S SHIFTS. ha-EVED ha-ivri ('the Hebrew SLAVE' — the man is demoted between tellings) asher heveta LANU ('whom YOU brought') — the husband still indicted; le-tzacheq BI now, not BANU: the mock-victim narrows from household to wife. The chet in segol per MS [G62-10, asserted]. The two-telling variance is the letter's own record of a rehearsed lie.

THE COMPOUND MARK [G62-10]. KA-HARIMI qoli — the he under the kaf carries sheva-and-patach (the compound half-vowel), checked in- stream [VERIFIED: manifest G62-10]; MS's accent-file on the verse (the books' merkha/tevir/tifcha shuffles on va-yaazov-bigdo-etzli) recorded named. etzli — 'beside ME': the garment's location testifies for her.

THE ANGER ON HEARSAY. va-yichar apo — the letter never says at whom; the reading tradition splits the anger (at Joseph with his wife's words / at the situation, knowing her — named): the machine records only the burning.

POTIPHAR'S OWN VERDICT [claim G62-15]. The reading takes the master's anger as directed not at Joseph but at the story — "I know you did not do it" — and reads the committal verb as an APPOINTMENT rather than a sentence, which is why the prison-keeper hands him the house within two verses. The machine records the custody with the master's disbelief carried beside it at witness tier, never as a tex…

THE PRISONERS' TWO SPELLINGS [G62-02/06]. meqom asher ASURE ha- melekh asurim — written with vav, read with yod: the FIRST of the Great Masorah's alphabet of vav-written yod-read words, carried in SNAPSHOT as the two-token pair [VERIFIED: manifest G62-02]; the Kitzur counts the sentence in it — ten years for the slander of ten brothers, two for the two remember-me's. And asurim ('bound') has exact…

THE REFRAIN INSIDE. va-yehi YHWH et yosef va-yet elav CHASED — the with-him formula crosses the prison wall intact; favor found again (chen, as at 39:4): the chapter's architecture repeats itself one level down.

THE CORRECTED WORD [G62-03]. et kal HA-ASIRIM — the printer muddled this token into the written/read list and Minchat Kohen followed; MS restores it with the Ramah, the Meiri, and the Hilleli's own note: yod after the samekh, lean second yod, no pair, marked unique — and SNAPSHOT writes exactly that [VERIFIED: manifest G62-03]. be-yad yosef — the hand-word completes its arc: prosperity, seized clo…

THE DROPPED HAND [G62-11]. va-asher hu ose YHWH MATZLIACH — the Kitzur: the closing refrain omits 'in his hand' (against 39:3), for in prison he had no business in his hand. roe et-kal: MS rules the et maqqefed without a stress-stroke — SNAPSHOT joins the maqqef but WRITES the meteg his books omit: pointing DISCREPANCY, filed [VERIFIED: G62-11]. The span ends with the doubled lie-demand still open…
